How Brazoria County, Texas Tax Sales

Brazoria County, Texas, organizes tax sales to collect unpaid property taxes and return delinquent properties to productive use. These sales, managed by the Brazoria County Sheriff’s Office, provide a transparent process for buyers while supporting county revenue needs. Here’s what you need to know.

Sale Schedule and Location

Tax foreclosure sales are held on the first Tuesday of each month, beginning at 10:00 a.m. Check out our Auction Calendar for scheduled auctions

Auctions take place in the Commissioners’ Courtroom on the 1st floor of the Brazoria County Courthouse.

Arrive early to review announcements or updates provided by auction officials.

Bidding and Payment Information

The starting bid includes delinquent taxes, penalties, interest, and related costs. Properties are awarded to the highest bidder who meets or exceeds the minimum bid.

Payment is required immediately after the auction.

Accepted forms of payment: cash, cashier’s check, or money order made payable to the Brazoria County Sheriff’s Office.

Personal or company checks are only accepted with a Letter of Guaranty from the bidder’s bank. Exact payments are required as no change will be provided.

Eligibility to Bid

Obtain a Statement of No Delinquent Tax from the Brazoria County Tax Office.

Submit a notarized request along with a $10 processing fee.

Submit requests at least 10 days before the sale to ensure timely processing.

The statement confirms the bidder does not owe taxes in Brazoria County, a requirement for participation.

Property Details and Responsibilities

The County Sell the Properties “as is,” without warranties on condition or title status.

Research each property thoroughly, including:

  1. Reviewing property records for liens or encumbrances.
  2. Confirming property location and accessibility.

Identifying any unpaid taxes not included in the minimum bid.

Taxing entities receive unsold properties (“struck off”) and may offer them for future sales.

Additional Considerations

  1. Registration: Confirm registration deadlines and requirements before the sale.
  2. Research Tools: Use county appraisal district resources to verify property details.
  3. Legal Assistance: Consider consulting a real estate attorney to navigate potential complexities, such as quiet title actions.
  4. Auction Rules: Familiarize yourself with all auction procedures to ensure compliance and avoid disqualification.

Preparing for a Successful Auction

  • Arrive early to understand the flow of the auction and review updates.
  • Bring all required documentation, including your Statement of No Delinquent Tax.
  • Ensure your payment method aligns with county requirements.
  • Plan for post-auction responsibilities, such as addressing any existing liens or completing quiet title actions if needed.
